## Decisions: what the team chose (hand-written, wins over generated facts)

## Contracts: how to reason about a failure class

Read one with `kit contract <name>` when its trigger applies.

| Contract                       | Applies when |
| ------------------------------ | ------------ |
| emit-hygiene                   | writing any code |
| logic-over-surface             | writing or reviewing a rule, contract, convention or skill |
| openapi-client-consumption     | touching a generated API client or the data it returns |
| self-descriptive-naming        | naming anything (file, class, function, variable, signal, route, token) |
| angular-tooling                | using, or failing to reach, the MCP server, the language server or the angular-developer skill |
| angular-version-targeting      | version upgrade, deprecation warnings, migrating an API |
| change-propagation             | new field, state update, input, mapping between layers |
| design-token-pattern           | colour, spacing, typography, theme, dark mode |
| layout-ownership               | padding, margin, scroll containers, sticky elements, host styles |
| library-theming-boundary       | styling a component from another library, or embedding one library in another |
| lifetime-matched-injection     | provider, providedIn, inject(), subscribe, timers, event listeners |
| reactive-boundary              | signal, RxJS, resource, effect, toSignal or toObservable |

## Priority on conflict (say the conflict out loud, never pick silently)

1. contract  2. decisions  3. conventions  4. angular-developer skill + MCP get_best_practices  5. your own knowledge

## Tools

- Framework question → `angular-developer` skill; version-dependent → MCP `get_best_practices` / `search_documentation`
- Symbol, references → LSP; if it does not answer → grep `.claude/.state/inventory.md`
- Template correctness → the build command in workspace.md (strictTemplates is off: also re-read changed templates)
- Tests → the test command in workspace.md
- A tool not available: say so once, use the fallback, keep working.

## Freshness

- `kit stale` lists conventions that no longer match the code. Stale ⇒ say so, then run `kit scan`.

## The loop

Look up the rules → ask the official layer for framework questions → build → LSP + build/test →
run the `codecraft` skill on the diff → report what was applied, skipped, and not checkable.
